content.text: The substantive indemnity triggers in both 11.1 and 11.2 are redacted ("[***]"), so I cannot verify IP/law/data-breach/misconduct coverage. Submitting needs_review.

input.quote: 11.2 Indemnification of AbbVie. Harpoon shall indemnify AbbVie, its Affiliates and its and their respective directors, officers, employees, and agents (the "AbbVie Indemnitees"), and defend and save each of them harmless, from and against any and all Losses in connection with any and all Third Party Claims incurred by or rendered against the AbbVie Indemnitees arising from or occurring as a result of: [***]
input.rationale:
Article 11 contains a genuine two-way indemnity architecture that already satisfies the structural preferred elements: Harpoon (counterparty) expressly indemnifies and defends AbbVie, its Affiliates and their personnel against Third Party Claims (11.2), and Sections 11.3, 11.4.1 and 11.4.4 supply the standard procedure (prompt written notice, indemnifying-Party assumption/control of the defence, and mandatory cooperation). This is not a one-way Customer indemnity and is not walk-away territory.

However, the operative trigger lists for both 11.2 (Harpoon's indemnity of AbbVie) and 11.1 (our reciprocal indemnity of Harpoon) are redacted as "[***]", so the substantive scope cannot be assessed from the four corners of the document. I therefore cannot confirm whether Harpoon's indemnity reaches third-party IP infringement claims, Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law, a data breach caused by Harpoon, or Harpoon's gross negligence/wilful misconduct, nor whether our own indemnity in 11.1 stays narrow (Customer-provided content and our breach of law) rather than sweeping in Harpoon's activities. Contextual signals cut in favour of some IP coverage — Section 7.4 gives AbbVie the first right to defend third-party patent infringement claims "Subject to Section 11.2", and p0471 refers to "a claim that may be subject to Section 11.2" and to "Harpoon['s] ... liab[ility] to indemnify any AbbVie Indemnitee" — but that is inference, not operative text.

Proposing a redline now would risk duplicating or contradicting the redacted triggers. Recommended next step: obtain the unredacted 11.1/11.2 trigger lists and confirm (a) Harpoon indemnity for Third Party Claims alleging that the Licensed Compounds/Licensed Products or Harpoon Technology infringe or misappropriate Third Party intellectual property (other than to the extent caused by AbbVie's modifications, combinations or specifications), and (b) that AbbVie's 11.1 indemnity is confined to AbbVie-supplied materials/information and AbbVie's breach of Applicable Law or this Agreement. Note also that Article 11 contains no monetary super-cap; the only limitation is the mutual consequential-damages exclusion in 11.5, which expressly carves out amounts payable to a Third Party under an Article 11 indemnity — that carve-out is favourable to us and is not flagged.

mappings.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
mappings.quote: Harpoon shall indemnify AbbVie, its Affiliates and its and their respective directors, officers, employees, and agents (the "AbbVie Indemnitees"), and defend and save each of them harmless

mappings.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
mappings.quote: from and against any and all Losses in connection with any and all Third Party Claims incurred by or rendered against the AbbVie Indemnitees

mappings.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
mappings.explanation: The trigger list in Section 11.2 is redacted ("arising from or occurring as a result of: [***]"), so IP-infringement coverage cannot be confirmed or drafted around without risking duplication of the redacted text. Section 7.4 and p0471 refer to third-party patent infringement claims against AbbVie as potentially "subject to Section 11.2", suggesting some coverage exists; unredacted text required.

mappings.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
mappings.explanation: Section 11.2's enumerated triggers are redacted; no other provision in the document states whether Harpoon indemnifies for its own breach of Applicable Law.

mappings.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
mappings.explanation: Section 11.2's enumerated triggers are redacted; Article 9 (Confidentiality) breach is carved out of the 11.5 damages exclusion but no visible text confirms an indemnity for a data/confidentiality breach caused by Harpoon.

mappings.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
mappings.explanation: Section 11.2's enumerated triggers are redacted. Gross negligence and wilful misconduct appear only in the 11.5 consequential-damages carve-out, which is not an indemnity trigger.

mappings.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
mappings.quote: The Indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice (an "Indemnification Claim Notice") of any Losses or discovery of fact upon which such Indemnified Party intends to base a request for indemnification under this Article 11

mappings.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
mappings.quote: at its option, the indemnifying Party may assume the defense of any Third Party Claim by giving written notice to the Indemnified Party within [***] after the indemnifying Party's receipt of an Indemnification Claim Notice

mappings.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
mappings.quote: the Indemnified Party shall, and shall cause each indemnitee to, cooperate in the defense or prosecution thereof and shall furnish such records, information and testimony, provide such witnesses and attend such conferences, discovery proceedings, hearings, trials and appeals as may be reasonably requested in connection therewith

mappings.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
mappings.explanation: Section 11.1 (our indemnity of the Harpoon Indemnitees) likewise ends in a redacted trigger list, so we cannot confirm that our exposure is confined to AbbVie-provided materials and AbbVie's breach of Applicable Law; unredacted text required before proposing any narrowing edit.
